transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because the doctor doing my insurance physical recently said my weight was too low. I don't really see it, honestly. To me, I just look lean from being up and down ladders and working long days painting. But they said I needed to follow up on it, so that's why I'm here.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss recently, or have you been losing weight without trying?

Well, I suppose I have lost some weight, but it's not exactly a mystery. I just don't eat all that much. Most days I keep it to coffee, and... maybe a protein bar between paint jobs. Then just a small dinner at night. Honestly, eating a full meal just feels like it would slow me down too much while I'm working. So the weight loss is probably just from doing that.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual or noticed any weakness, even when you're not working long hours?
No, not really. I mean, sure, I'm tired at the end of a long day, but that's just the job. When I'm off the clock, I feel fine. I haven't noticed any weird weakness or anything like that.
Have you had any problems with your appetite, or any nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain that might be affecting how much you eat?

No, nothing like that. I don't have any stomach pain or nausea, and I definitely haven't been throwing up or anything. As for my appetite... I mean, I get hungry, I just sort of ignore it while I'm working. So it's not that I can't eat because my stomach hurts, I just choose to keep it light. Everything works fine in that department.
Have you ever been told that your weight was too low before, or is this the first time someone has mentioned it as a concern?

Well, actually, that's kind of why I came in. I had to do an insurance physical recently, and the doctor there told me my weight was too low. Before that, no, nobody really mentioned it. 

Honestly, to me, I just look lean. I mean, I spend all day climbing up and down ladders and working long hours, so... I just figure that's what a guy in my line of work is supposed to look like. But yeah, the insurance doctor is the one who brought it up as a concern.
Do you worry about gaining weight or becoming fat, even though others may tell you that you're underweight?

Well, yeah, I guess I do. I mean, even if that doctor said I'm too low, I still... I don't want to get fat. Like, if I have to go to a client dinner or I end up eating something heavy, like bread, and I see the scale go up even just a little bit the next morning... I get pretty tense about it. I usually start cutting back right away the next day just to make sure it doesn't stick. I just want to keep it under control.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to exercise or stick to certain eating rules to keep from gaining weight, even if others might say you're already thin?

Not really. I don't go to a gym or run or anything like that. Climbing ladders and hauling paint around all day is plenty of a workout on its own, so I don't really need to add extra exercise on top of it. 

And as for eating rules... I don't have a specific diet plan or a list of things I absolutely can't eat. Like I mentioned, I just try to keep my meals light while I'm working, and if I feel like I overdid it, I just eat a little less the next day to balance it out. But I don't really go out of my way to follow a strict regimen or anything.
Do you ever restrict how much you eat, even when you're hungry, to keep from gaining weight?

Yeah, I suppose I do. I mean, most days I just keep it to coffee in the morning, and maybe a protein bar between paint jobs. Then I'll just have a small dinner when I get home. 

Even if my stomach is grumbling while I'm working, I don't really stop to eat a big lunch. Eating a full meal just feels like it would slow me down and make me feel heavy on the ladders. So, yeah, I just stick to keeping it light to keep things in check.
Does your concern about your weight or eating interfere with your daily life, like causing you a lot of stress, affecting your work, or making it hard to be around friends and family?

Well, it doesn't really affect my work. I'm still getting all my painting jobs done, no problem there. But... I guess it does affect things outside of work. Like, I'll avoid going to client dinners if I can, or I'll skip out on social plans with friends. It's just easier that way. I don't want to deal with a situation where people start commenting on what I'm eating, or telling me how I look. It just causes too much stress, so I usually just stay away from those kinds of gatherings.
Would you say you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you're already underweight?

Yeah, I suppose I do. I mean... if I step on the scale and it goes up even just a little bit, like after one of those client dinners I can't get out of, or if I end up eating something with bread... I definitely get pretty tense about it. I just immediately start cutting back the next day to make sure the weight doesn't stick. So, yeah, I really don't want to put on weight.
Do you see yourself as overweight or in need of weight control even when other people say you're already thin or underweight?

Well, people do tell me I'm thin, but I just don't see it that way. I definitely feel like I need to keep things under control. 

Like, when I catch myself in a mirror, or if I'm looking at photos of myself standing next to one of my murals... I basically judge my whole day by whether my stomach and my face look sharp enough. If they look soft or round at all, it just ruins it for me. So, yeah, regardless of what anyone else says about my size, I still feel a strong need to manage how I look.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests possible underweight etiology including nutritional deficiency or eating disorder.

The patient denied symptoms of fatigue, weakness, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain, which makes E40, E41, and E43 less likely. The focus remains on unintentional weight loss and possible eating behaviors, keeping R63.4 and F50.0 as likely candidates.

This supports an eating disorder presentation.
